facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence for lower risk is that 2026 behaviour has favoured creditors and that two large counterparties share the legacy burden. Chemours has no sponsor to extract cash, bought no shares in 2024, 2025 or the first nine months of 2026, cut the annualised dividend rate by 65.00% from 2024 and repaid euro term debt of a size close to its asset-sale proceeds, while DuPont and Corteva funded USD 150 million into escrow and carry half of qualified PFAS costs; internal control over financial reporting was effective at year-end 2025. The view would move towards low if the proxy statement shows an independent board, the amended annual report shows no new deficiency, the securities claims are dismissed and the AFFF personal-injury claims settle within the remaining USD 1,130 million of cost-sharing capacity. It would move towards high if the credit agreement shows wide dividend or investment capacity that is then used, if a regulator or court action follows the 2024 review, if PFAS losses exceed the cost-sharing cap, or if the cost-sharing parties cannot meet their half. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 162; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–39; 10-K_2025-12-31_cc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 155; calculation C7

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Near-term liquidity is adequate, and the 2028 wall is the pressure point. Cash and undrawn revolver gave USD 1,651 million of liquidity at September 30, 2026, of which USD 220 million of commitments matured on October 7, 2026, leaving at most USD 1,431 million if nothing is drawn; payments of USD 780 million fall due in 2028 and USD 647 million in 2029, USD 1,427 million together, and the revolver matures early if the 2028 debt is not refinanced within 91 days of maturity, so refinancing has to come before the revolver can be relied on. Cash was USD 698 million at the balance sheet date, of which USD 410 million, or 58.74%, is held at foreign subsidiaries; the dividend payable on December 15, 2026 takes USD 13.17 million, and the effect of the USD 51 million North Carolina payment on cash is not established because its funding source is not stated. Management states that liquidity is sufficient to settle current liabilities through at least the end of November 2027, and warns that an adverse legal or environmental outcome could materially affect it. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence for a stronger credit is that earnings are guided to recover and that 2026 behaviour has favoured lenders: the company guides fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of USD 160 million to USD 185 million and full-year net leverage below 4.2x, it has no sponsor to extract cash, bought no shares and cut the annualised dividend rate by 65.00%, 61.44% of contractual debt payments fall after 2030, and it refinanced the 2027 notes in March 2026. The view would improve if full-year Adjusted EBITDA reaches the outlook of USD 775 million to USD 800 million, the euro term loan and 2028 notes are refinanced before the springing-maturity window opens, and the AFFF claims settle within the remaining USD 1,130 million of cost-sharing capacity. It would worsen if fourth-quarter earnings fall below the guided range, titanium dioxide pricing reverses, refrigerant earnings keep falling, revolver availability after October 7, 2026 proves lower than USD 733 million, or PFAS losses outrun the cost-sharing cap. facts.label: Company description
facts.text: Chemours earns its cash from three product families sold into regulation-driven and cyclical markets: refrigerants and thermal solutions (Thermal & Specialized Solutions), titanium dioxide pigment (Titanium Technologies) and fluoropolymer materials (Advanced Performance Materials). In fiscal 2025 they were 35.57%, 41.82% and 21.75% of net sales of USD 5,808 million, and in the nine months to September 30, 2026 36.99%, 42.09% and 20.08%, so the sales mix is balanced but earnings are not. The business supports cash-flow visibility only in part: refrigerant sales follow a regulatory transition and a seasonal cooling season, titanium dioxide follows construction and packaging demand, and the company's own legacy-site liabilities attach to plants that remain in operation, which limits liquidity preservation and keeps refinancing confidence tied to earnings recovery. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C15

facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: Chemours is a widely held public company with no controlling shareholder or sponsor identified, so there is no owner able to extract cash or to inject equity, and the proxy statement that would show large holders and board independence was not supplied. Debt sits at the parent and is guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries; the last guarantor-group summary covered fiscal 2025 and showed obligor net sales of 67.99% of group net sales, so at least 32.01% is earned outside the obligor group, a floor because intercompany sales inflate the obligor total. The 2034 notes carry a guarantee from a guarantor that no filing names, so the current perimeter is not established, and receivables are sold through a non-guarantor special purpose entity, so Structural priority must settle how claims rank. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; calculation C21

facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is cyclical and policy-driven rather than recurring. Opteon sales jumped in 2025 on stationary air conditioning volumes tied to the AIM Act and fell in 2026 as the initial channel fill faded; nine-month net sales were flat as a 3% price gain offset a 3% volume fall, and Titanium Technologies lifted price 10% in the third quarter while volume rose 1%. Pricing power is real where regulation or quality limits substitutes, but the Opteon composition patents expire through the end of the decade and titanium dioxide demand is about 73.00% of nameplate capacity, so price gains depend on discipline rather than structure. Pigment grades are not fully substitutable because of quality consistency and specialty fluoropolymers are chosen for performance in demanding uses, but the filings give no retention or contract-duration data, so switching costs are not established; one pigment customer takes more than 20% of segment sales, which concentrates revenue risk in the segment meant to offset refrigerants. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Margins are defended poorly under volume pressure. Cost of goods sold rose 4% in the third quarter on higher fixed costs and lower production rates while sales rose 3%, gross margin for nine months fell 0.50 percentage points to 16.16%, and Thermal & Specialized Solutions margin dropped to 27% from 35%; Titanium Technologies margin recovered to 13% from 4% on price. Energy is about 10% of titanium dioxide production cost and the company buys its titanium ore, chlorine and calcined petroleum coke from outside suppliers, with its own mines supplying under 10% of ore needs, so input shocks pass through unless priced. The chlorine plan for the DeLisle plant is not stated after the supply agreement ended in March 2026, and no fixed and variable cost split is supplied, so downside cost flexibility beyond capital spending and the dividend is not established. facts.label: Capital intensity and cash conversion
facts.text: Capital spending is flexible but is being held below depreciation. Twelve-month spending of USD 189 million is 59.25% of depreciation and amortization of USD 319 million, nine-month spending fell 14.29% and the outlook of USD 220 million to USD 230 million implies a larger fourth quarter. Conversion is low: free cash flow was 28.36% of adjusted EBITDA, interest expense takes 36.83% of adjusted EBITDA, supplier finance obligations rose to USD 151 million from USD 132 million at year-end 2025, and legacy settlements and a USD 90 million capitalised commitment under the Consent Decree sit on top. EBITDA therefore translates into limited cash for debt reduction, and the 2028 payments of USD 780 million are about 3.70x twelve-month free cash flow. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is intense where capacity exceeds demand and moderate where patents protect. Refrigerant competitors include Solstice Advanced Materials, Arkema, Orbia, Daikin and Chinese producers, titanium dioxide competitors include Tronox, LB Group, Kronos and INEOS, and titanium dioxide demand is 73.00% of nameplate capacity, which caps price. New entry is limited by chloride process know-how, patents to the end of the decade for the main Opteon molecule and regulatory product approvals; substitutes are regulatory (the shift from older refrigerants) rather than competing products, and pigment grades are not fully substitutable. Buyers are fragmented at group level but concentrated in pigment, where the ten largest customers take more than 44% of sales, and supplier power is moderate: titanium ore comes from several suppliers on contracts and can be mixed across sites, chlorine and energy follow regional price cycles, and fluorspar and chlorinated organics are sourced from many suppliers. For creditors this means refrigerant earnings are protected only until patents lapse and pigment earnings depend on price discipline. facts.label: Macro, regulatory and technology factors
facts.text: These factors are material to credit. The AIM Act transition drove the 2025 Opteon surge and its 2026 fade, and the European fluorinated-gas rules support growth; PFAS regulation and litigation drive the settlements and the Consent Decree; trade policy and tariffs are managed through pricing and sourcing; construction and packaging demand set titanium dioxide volumes; and data centre cooling and semiconductor demand lift Performance solutions, whose nine-month net sales rose 7.32%. The telomer-based exit of a specialty business shows that regulation can strand products, and the annual report describes commercialisation of a next-generation refrigerant for data centre cooling as pending regulatory approvals. facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: Scale and market position is average: large and leading in two product families but exposed to price in both. Competitive advantage is average, resting on patents that expire through the end of the decade and process know-how whose cost position is management's own claim. Business diversification is average, because sales are balanced across segments while earnings depend on refrigerants. Cost and capex flexibility is average, with capital spending held below depreciation but largely fixed costs and a fixed environmental commitment. Margin stability is weak, shown by the swing in refrigerant and titanium dioxide margins. Free cash flow stability is weak, with negative free cash flow in fiscal 2024 and USD 211 million over the latest twelve months that includes escrowed receipts. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average: the market took the 2034 issue in March 2026 at a higher coupon, but one agency lowered its rating by one notch in July 2026 and the 2028 wall is close. Liquidity position is average: it is strong against the 2026 and 2027 payments but only adequate once the 2028 and 2029 payments are counted and with most cash held abroad. Financial policy and governance is average, with restrained distributions and no sponsor offset by the unresolved 2024 review and legal exposure. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 149; calculation C7; calculation C8

facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next 12 to 24 months the company outlook is for fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of USD 160 million to USD 185 million, a full-year range of USD 775 million to USD 800 million, capital spending of USD 220 million to USD 230 million and net leverage below 4.2x, with positive free cash flow in the fourth quarter. Tailwinds are titanium dioxide price momentum, order strength for Performance solutions products in data centre and semiconductor uses, and continued adoption of low global warming refrigerants under the AIM Act and European rules; headwinds are the fading stationary air conditioning aftermarket, annual settlement payments, tariffs, and the 2028 refinancing window opening within about 18 months. Over three to five years the Opteon patents lapse by the end of the decade, New Jersey payments are funded from escrow to 2030, and cost-sharing capacity is largely consumed, so the credit has to be sustained by earnings and market access rather than by disposals or counterparties. facts.label: Qualitative downside scenario
facts.text: The scenario starts with titanium dioxide price gains fading because demand stays near 73.00% of capacity while refrigerant aftermarket volume keeps falling. The first operational break is lower volume at the refrigerant plants and weaker price realisation in pigment, which lifts unit cost because the cost base is largely fixed. Adjusted EBITDA falls by USD 100 million to USD 644 million, net leverage reaches 4.87x on net debt held at USD 3,135 million (USD 3,148.17 million pro forma for the declared dividend) and interest cover falls to 2.35x, while settlement payments continue. Management levers are capital spending, which is already below depreciation, the dividend of about USD 52.69 million a year and working capital; disposals are exhausted because the land sales are complete. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027 because only USD 68 million falls due in 2026 and 2027 and liquidity is about USD 1,431 million, but it would not hold leverage near current levels, and a refinancing in 2028 would be priced from a weaker position with the revolver's early maturity at stake. Observable triggers are fourth-quarter earnings below USD 160 million, pigment price reversal and revolver availability below USD 733 million. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-02_cc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C3; calculation C6; calculation C12; calculation C14; calculation C17; calculation C18

facts.text: Overall, Chemours presents an adequate but concentrated business profile supported by leading refrigerant and pigment positions, near-term liquidity that covers the 2026 and 2027 payments and cost sharing for legacy liabilities, but credit quality is constrained by high leverage, thin interest cover and unquantified PFAS exposure. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow is small after interest, capital spending and settlements. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on titanium dioxide pricing, refrigerant earnings holding up and the 2028 debt being addressed before the revolver's early-maturity window opens. The primary downside path is a fall in refrigerant and pigment earnings that lifts leverage while settlement payments continue. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and covenant levels, the amended annual report, the proxy statement, peer and market data, and cash interest for 2026. Top risk: refrigerant and titanium dioxide earnings falling before the 2028 refinancing. Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7; calculation C14

## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied filings and releases support a source-based credit assessment of Chemours Co through the Q3 2026 balance sheet, but not covenant, security or controls conclusions, which creditors should treat as provisional until missing documents arrive.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–6; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_cc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 1–5

Four gaps set that limit. No executed credit agreement or indenture was supplied, so covenant definitions and the temporarily raised maintenance level rest on the filings' own summaries. The amendment to the 2025 annual report that the latest quarterly filing cites is absent, so what it changes, including in controls, is not established. Cash-paid interest and taxes are printed for 2025 but not for the 2026 interim periods, apart from one property-sale tax item. Revolver availability at quarter end still counts commitments that matured in October 2026.

Supplied handoff: Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 b24b4904b55ecf2403f7a8ea82234e910f8aa934874f9a1576daecfc2617c1b4.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage is easing but remains high: net debt is 4.21x issuer-adjusted EBITDA for the twelve months to September 30, 2026, against 4.67x at year-end 2025, so creditors still depend on earnings recovery and refinancing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_cc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_cc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 161–162; calculation C39; calculation C38

Net debt fell by USD 336 million while adjusted EBITDA stayed at USD 743 million and USD 744 million; the fall is close to the USD 342 million of asset-sale proceeds, so it mostly reflects a one-time disposal. Reported EBITDA, which carries litigation charges and a USD 316 million asset-sale gain, puts net leverage at 4.31x. Liquidity was USD 698 million of cash and USD 953 million of revolver availability at quarter end, but USD 220 million of those commitments matured on October 7, 2026, and cash interest cover is not printed for 2026.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 149; calculation C36; calculation C40; calculation C44

### Leverage and coverage

Leverage on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA improved because net debt fell, not because earnings grew: twelve-month adjusted EBITDA was USD 743 million at year-end 2025 and USD 744 million at September 30, 2026, while net debt dropped by USD 336 million, taking net leverage from 4.67x to 4.21x. The reduction rests on asset-sale proceeds of USD 342 million, so it is not repeatable from operations, and adjusted EBITDA is exposed to the thermal and specialized solutions business, whose nine-month Segment Adjusted EBITDA of USD 539 million was flat against USD 542 million but whose third-quarter figure fell to USD 136 million from USD 194 million. Coverage is thin: 2025 EBITDA over cash interest was 1.32x on reported EBITDA and 2.96x on adjusted EBITDA, and interim cover cannot be stated because cash interest is not printed.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-02_cc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_cc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 130–133; 10-K_2025-12-31_cc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163; calculation C36; calculation C38; calculation C39
### Liquidity and maturities

Cash of USD 698 million and revolver availability of USD 953 million gave USD 1,651 million of liquidity at September 30, 2026. USD 220 million of the commitments behind that availability matured on October 7, 2026 and no later availability is stated, so forward liquidity is lower than the quarter-end figure by up to that amount. Contractual payments are small until 2028, when USD 780 million falls due, including the 2028 senior notes and the euro term loan; the revolver has a springing maturity if either term loan or the 2028 and 2029 notes are not refinanced within 91 days before they mature, so the 2028 wall also governs revolver access.
### Cash-flow quality and funding float

Free cash flow for the twelve months to September 30, 2026 was USD 211 million after USD 189 million of capital spending, but nine-month operating cash flow of USD 263 million includes the USD 150 million PFAS insurance receipt held as restricted cash for New Jersey settlement payments, and USD 103 million of restricted cash, mainly that escrow, remains, so free cash flow overstates what is free for debt service. Settlement payments continue: the New Jersey order totals USD 875 million over 25 years and the North Carolina settlement USD 455 million over 15 years across all settling companies, with Chemours bearing its cost-sharing share, which the 10-Q puts at USD 176 million for the remaining New Jersey payments on a net present value basis. Working-capital funding that is not debt adds to the risk: supplier finance obligations were USD 151 million against USD 132 million at year-end 2025, customer-facilitated programs accelerated USD 258 million of receivables in the nine months, and receivable sales through the securitization and European factoring facilities are accounted for as sales, so withdrawal of any program would draw on cash and revolver availability.
### Data quality and definitions

Chemours states no unadjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is derived from income before income taxes, interest and depreciation, and the twelve-month figure of USD 727 million carries a USD 316 million asset-sale gain and litigation and environmental charges that the issuer's adjusted figure of USD 744 million removes. The annual report's segment reconciliation builds USD 750 million for 2025 against the releases' USD 743 million, a USD 7 million difference equal to the inventory write-offs the note lists as a separate item, which is consistent with the releases not adding them back. Prior-period figures are revised, and the amended annual report filed on November 3, 2026 is not supplied. Events after quarter end are flagged with their dates and kept out of period figures: the revolver tranche that matured on October 7, 2026, the interest rate swaps that matured on October 31, 2026, the first North Carolina settlement payment in October 2026 and the dividend declared on October 27, 2026.

spans.text: # Chemours Co (cc): business and governance, as of 2026-11-05
## Request

Business and governance for Chemours Co (issuer cc), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the company and its segments, ownership and control, transactions and new debt issues, legacy-liability relationships and governance conduct, drawn from the 2025 annual report, the first and third quarter 2026 reports and the third quarter 2026 earnings release.
## Sources

Supplied handoff: Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 b24b4904b55ecf2403f7a8ea82234e910f8aa934874f9a1576daecfc2617c1b4.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Chemours has no controlling shareholder or sponsor, so creditors depend on the company's own financial policy and on legacy-cost sharing with DuPont and Corteva, and governance risk is medium rather than low because of open regulatory inquiries and unquantified PFAS claims.

Financial policy has favoured debt reduction in 2026: the company said land-sale proceeds would reduce debt and repaid euro term debt of a similar size, share repurchases remain dormant and the dividend rate is 65.00% below 2024. Business risk matters as much as governance risk, because Thermal & Specialized Solutions supplied 72.25% of segment Adjusted EBITDA in the first nine months of 2026 while its third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA fell 30%.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_cc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 162; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 133; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_cc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C7; calculation C4; calculation C10
### Key findings

- Ownership gives creditors neither a sponsor to fear nor a sponsor to rely on. The filings name no controlling holder, the table of large holders sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied, and no equity injection or cure right is described, so support in stress would have to come from the public market.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-K_2025-12-31_cc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 145; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Earnings depend on refrigerants and on one titanium dioxide price cycle. Thermal & Specialized Solutions produced 72.25% of nine-month segment Adjusted EBITDA (USD 539 million of USD 746 million), Titanium Technologies 20.38% and Advanced Performance Materials 7.37%. In the third quarter refrigerant earnings fell 30% to USD 136 million as the aftermarket fill faded, while titanium dioxide earnings rose to USD 85 million from USD 25 million on price.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 133; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_cc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation C4; calculation C14

- Customer concentration is a Titanium Technologies issue rather than a group issue. No customer exceeds 10% of group net sales, but one titanium dioxide customer takes more than 20% of that segment's sales, which is more than 8.36% of group net sales, and the ten largest take more than 44%, so a loss or repricing at one account would move segment earnings.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_cc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C5

- Legacy PFAS and environmental liabilities are the main source of event risk and are only partly quantified. Accrued litigation rose to USD 553 million from USD 484 million at year-end 2025; New Jersey will draw USD 875 million over 25 years and North Carolina USD 455 million over 15 years across all settling parties; the 2026 Consent Decree adds a USD 23 million penalty, USD 90 million of project funding and USD 136 million of environmental reserves. The company states that losses on the large water, personal-injury and state natural-resource matters cannot be estimated, so accruals may understate the cash that will be needed.

- Cost sharing with DuPont and Corteva is a real offset, but it is capped, mostly used or committed, and depends on two counterparties whose finances were not reviewed. Chemours bears half of qualified spend up to USD 4,000 million; USD 1,130 million remained after insurance recoveries and settlement present values, so 71.75% of the cap is used or committed, and the same parties funded USD 150 million into escrow for New Jersey payments in return for Chemours' insurance rights on the first USD 300 million of recoveries. After the cap or 2040, Chemours' indemnities continue unchanged.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34–39; calculation C16

- Governance carries an unresolved history that the filings do not close. The 2024 Audit Committee review found breaches of the code of ethics for senior executive and finance positions, the SEC and a U.S. Attorney's office have open requests, a 2024 securities class action was dismissed in May 2026 with leave to amend and was repleaded, and a class action filed in October 2026 targets 2026 statements on Opteon demand and guidance. Internal control was effective at year-end 2025 after the 2023 weaknesses were remediated in 2024, but the amended annual report filed on November 3, 2026 was not supplied.

- Financial policy in 2026 has favoured debt reduction, at a higher coupon and with covenant relief behind it. Asset-sale proceeds of USD 342 million sat beside a euro term loan paydown equal to 94.74% of that amount; USD 700 million of notes due 2034 refinanced the 2027 notes and part of the 2028 notes and add USD 17.71 million a year of coupon; the regular dividend continues at a rate 65.00% below 2024; repurchases have been dormant since 2023; and the 2025 amendments raised the leverage test through September 2026 and the dollar term loan margin by 50 bp.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for lower risk is that 2026 behaviour has favoured creditors and that two large counterparties share the legacy burden. Chemours has no sponsor to extract cash, bought no shares in 2024, 2025 or the first nine months of 2026, cut the annualised dividend rate by 65.00% from 2024 and repaid euro term debt of a size close to its asset-sale proceeds, while DuPont and Corteva funded USD 150 million into escrow and carry half of qualified PFAS costs; internal control over financial reporting was effective at year-end 2025. The view would move towards low if the proxy statement shows an independent board, the amended annual report shows no new deficiency, the securities claims are dismissed and the AFFF personal-injury claims settle within the remaining USD 1,130 million of cost-sharing capacity. It would move towards high if the credit agreement shows wide dividend or investment capacity that is then used, if a regulator or court action follows the 2024 review, if PFAS losses exceed the cost-sharing cap, or if the cost-sharing parties cannot meet their half.
### Limitations

- The amended annual report filed on November 3, 2026 was not supplied, so the controls and reporting-quality view uses the original annual report and the third quarter report and would weaken if the amendment reports a deficiency or a restatement.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 183; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The credit agreement and indentures were not supplied, so the capacity to pay dividends, repurchase shares, sell assets or move value to non-guarantors is not tested, which keeps this module from separating legal capacity from willingness and holds the risk level at medium.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 211; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Loss estimates for most PFAS claims are not stated and the financial strength of DuPont and Corteva was not reviewed, so the offset from cost sharing could be smaller than shown and the risk level could rise.
- Customer names, contract terms and cost structure are stated only through concentration percentages and an energy share, so the business view cannot test how durable titanium dioxide earnings are.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Chemours has no acquisition, sponsor buyout or recapitalisation in fiscal 2025 or 2026; the transactions that matter to creditors are a refinancing, asset sales and settlements. On March 12, 2026 it issued USD 700 million of senior notes due 2034, guaranteed by a guarantor that the filings do not name, and used the proceeds with cash to redeem all USD 495 million of the 2027 notes and USD 188 million of the 2028 notes. That extended maturities but added USD 17.71 million a year of coupon on the replaced debt.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 187; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C8

Asset sales then reduced floating-rate secured debt. Sales of Kuan Yin land parcels brought USD 356 million of consideration against about USD 360 million agreed, with nine parcels sold in April 2026 and the last in September 2026, and the company repaid EUR 280 million, about USD 324 million, of its euro term loan in nine months, leaving EUR 135 million. Total debt principal fell by USD 310 million to USD 3,872 million between year-end 2025 and September 30, 2026.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C17

Lender-facing terms changed in 2025. The May amendment raised the leverage test through the quarter ended September 30, 2026 and extended USD 780 million of revolving commitments to May 2030, and the October amendment moved the dollar term loan maturity to October 2032 at a margin 50 bp higher. USD 220 million of revolving commitments matured on October 7, 2026, after the quarter end. The New Jersey and North Carolina settlements and the 2026 Consent Decree are legal claims on cash rather than financing choices, and their amounts are set out under key findings.

spans.text: # Chemours Co (cc): fundamental credit, as of 2026-11-05
## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for Chemours Co (issuer cc), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business quality, financial profile, liquidity and refinancing, governance, downside path and monitoring, drawn from the 2025 annual report, the third quarter 2026 report and release, and the source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance results of this run.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_cc-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K of The Chemours Company for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-24 (signature date; filing date not stated) | adf80f4588f501b9f797e1b55a5853888465c5d9b30aef8ff07b3cd4340b3957 | Business and competitive description, patents, raw materials, customers, industry demand, guarantor summary, segment results |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q of The Chemours Company for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | 2026-11-05 (signature date; filing date not stated) | f23013a765ad5943b395240230ccfbe7a0cca417e186c8a1a82b34a215485de7 | Debt and revolver terms, cost of goods sold commentary, capital spending, ratings statement, segment results |

| EX-99.1_2026-11-02_cc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl | Press release (Exhibit 99.1) reporting third quarter 2026 results | 2026-11-02 | d716a94a423338ae97b02c515014fccad1457c8952131fe6a67cf2f82a22b1e0 | Segment results, adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, issuer net leverage, fourth quarter and full-year 2026 outlook |
Supplied handoff: Source readiness (CP-0), sha256 b24b4904b55ecf2403f7a8ea82234e910f8aa934874f9a1576daecfc2617c1b4.
Supplied handoff: Financial foundation (CP-1), sha256 ad869fb2a7b9fef91c7fcbad7a5a9c55d4a476c0b5b51d9f754e756a36962cec.
Supplied handoff: Business & governance (CP-1A), sha256 b2f4b1d9289772d6e2af279ed0cf37808937334b66320b0ba03d62da0cf30439.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Chemours is a stretched but liquid credit: leverage is high and fell in 2026 only through an asset sale, while PFAS settlements, the 2028 maturity wall and a normalising refrigerant business leave little margin for error.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2

Creditors depend on a titanium dioxide price recovery, on cost sharing with DuPont and Corteva that is already 71.75% used or committed, and on refinancing USD 780 million due in 2028 and USD 647 million in 2029. Liquidity of USD 1,431 million after the matured revolver tranche is about equal to those two years of payments, but only if the revolver stays available, and covenant headroom cannot be tested.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C16
### Key findings

- Leverage is high and the 2026 improvement is one-time. Net leverage fell to 4.21x from 4.67x on issuer-adjusted EBITDA, with net debt of USD 3,135 million at September 30, 2026, but net debt fell USD 336 million against USD 342 million of asset-sale proceeds while twelve-month adjusted EBITDA stayed at USD 744 million, so the gain will not repeat from operations; on the issuer's principal basis the ratio is 4.27x, which the issuer states as approximately 4.3x. After the dividend declared on October 27, 2026, pro forma net debt is USD 3,148.17 million and pro forma net leverage on reported EBITDA is 4.33x; the effect of the October 2026 North Carolina payment on net debt, and pro forma leverage on adjusted EBITDA, are not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-02_cc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 13; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_cc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

- Interest cover is thin, and the 2026 refinancing made it thinner. Adjusted EBITDA covers interest expense 2.72x over the twelve months (2.65x on reported EBITDA), cover of cash interest in 2025 was 1.32x on reported and 2.96x on adjusted EBITDA, and the 2034 notes add about USD 17.71 million a year of coupon; cash interest for the 2026 interim periods is not printed, so the cash measure is not established for 2026.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 317; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 133; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C4; calculation C5

- Near-term liquidity is adequate, and the 2028 wall is the pressure point. Cash and undrawn revolver gave USD 1,651 million of liquidity at September 30, 2026, of which USD 220 million of commitments matured on October 7, 2026, leaving at most USD 1,431 million if nothing is drawn; payments of USD 780 million fall due in 2028 and USD 647 million in 2029, USD 1,427 million together, and the revolver matures early if the 2028 debt is not refinanced within 91 days of maturity, so refinancing has to come before the revolver can be relied on. Cash was USD 698 million at the balance sheet date, of which USD 410 million, or 58.74%, is held at foreign subsidiaries; the dividend payable on December 15, 2026 takes USD 13.17 million, and the effect of the USD 51 million North Carolina payment on cash is not established because its funding source is not stated. Management states that liquidity is sufficient to settle current liabilities through at least the end of November 2027, and warns that an adverse legal or environmental outcome could materially affect it.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C12; calculation C24

- Free cash flow is small and overstates cash free for debt service. Twelve-month free cash flow was USD 211 million after USD 189 million of capital spending, equal to 27.05% of the 2028 payments, but nine-month operating cash flow includes the USD 150 million PFAS insurance receipt held as restricted cash, and settlement payments in New Jersey, North Carolina and under the Consent Decree continue for 15 to 25 years.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-02_cc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C8; calculation C16

- Earnings are concentrated in refrigerants, which are normalising, while titanium dioxide and advanced materials move differently. Thermal & Specialized Solutions supplied 72.25% of nine-month segment Adjusted EBITDA, its third-quarter figure fell 30% to USD 136 million, Titanium Technologies rose to USD 85 million from USD 25 million on a 10% price increase, and Advanced Performance Materials fell 42.71% over nine months. The fourth-quarter outlook of USD 160 million to USD 185 million is 25.00% to 44.53% above the prior-year quarter, which would help, but it is a company projection.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-02_cc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_cc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C9; calculation C15

- Margins have little cushion because production costs are largely fixed in the short run and key inputs are bought from third parties. Cost of goods sold rose 4% in the third quarter against a 3% rise in net sales, which the company attributes to higher fixed costs and lower production rates, gross margin for nine months was 16.16% against 16.66%, and the sources give no split between fixed and variable cost, so operating leverage is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 139; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C19

- Governance and legacy liabilities, not a sponsor, set the downside. Accrued litigation rose by USD 69 million to USD 553 million, 71.75% of the cost-sharing cap is used or committed, claims such as the AFFF personal-injury cases carry no loss estimate, and the 2024 review, open regulatory requests and an amended annual report that was not supplied keep governance risk at medium.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C16

- The primary downside path runs from refrigerant and titanium dioxide earnings to the 2028 refinancing. With net debt held at USD 3,135 million (USD 3,148.17 million pro forma for the declared dividend), net leverage reaches 4.87x if adjusted EBITDA falls by USD 100 million and 5.00x at USD 627 million, a fall of 15.73%, while interest cover at USD 644 million of EBITDA is 2.35x; the settlement payments would continue throughout.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3; calculation C14
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence for a stronger credit is that earnings are guided to recover and that 2026 behaviour has favoured lenders: the company guides fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of USD 160 million to USD 185 million and full-year net leverage below 4.2x, it has no sponsor to extract cash, bought no shares and cut the annualised dividend rate by 65.00%, 61.44% of contractual debt payments fall after 2030, and it refinanced the 2027 notes in March 2026. The view would improve if full-year Adjusted EBITDA reaches the outlook of USD 775 million to USD 800 million, the euro term loan and 2028 notes are refinanced before the springing-maturity window opens, and the AFFF claims settle within the remaining USD 1,130 million of cost-sharing capacity. It would worsen if fourth-quarter earnings fall below the guided range, titanium dioxide pricing reverses, refrigerant earnings keep falling, revolver availability after October 7, 2026 proves lower than USD 733 million, or PFAS losses outrun the cost-sharing cap.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-02_cc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_cc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 6; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9; calculation C17; calculation C18
### Limitations

- Chemours states no unadjusted EBITDA and its adjusted measure excludes recurring litigation and environmental charges, so the leverage and cover conclusions use issuer-adjusted earnings and would look weaker on a measure that keeps those charges, on which net leverage is higher at 4.31x, or 4.33x pro forma for the dividend declared on October 27, 2026.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-02_cc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 12

- No compliance certificate or covenant calculation is available and the raised leverage test ended with the quarter to September 30, 2026, so the liquidity and refinancing conclusions cannot test whether a maintenance covenant becomes binding after that date.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; Source readiness (CP-0)

- The 2026 outlook and the fourth-quarter outlook are company projections and no forward credit model was built, so the improvement path in the contrary evidence rests on guidance that could be missed.

### Strengths and weaknesses

Near-term liquidity is the strongest support. Cash and undrawn revolver of USD 1,651 million at September 30, 2026, and at most USD 1,431 million after the October 7, 2026 maturity, sit against payments of only USD 26 million in 2026 and USD 42 million in 2027, so liquidity distress before the 2028 wall would need a sharp earnings or legal shock.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6; calculation C18

Scale and leading positions in refrigerants and titanium dioxide support the business. Net sales of USD 5,808 million come from three segments and no customer exceeds 10% of group net sales, which cushions a shock to any one product line, although the earnings mix is far more concentrated than the sales mix.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C15

Deleveraging and maturity extension in 2026 reduced risk. Net debt fell USD 336 million, the 2027 notes were redeemed with the 2034 issue and the euro term loan was cut by EUR 280 million, so the nearest unsecured maturity is now 2028, at the cost of a higher coupon.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C2; calculation C5

Cost sharing with DuPont and Corteva halves the net legacy burden within the cap. The counterparties carry half of qualified PFAS spend up to USD 4,000 million and funded USD 150 million of escrow for New Jersey payments, which keeps settlements affordable for Chemours alone for now.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C16

Distribution restraint keeps cash in the business. The annualised dividend rate is 65.00% below 2024, there have been no repurchases since 2023 and there is no sponsor to extract value, so cash is not leaving while leverage is high.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C17

High leverage and thin interest cover are the first weakness. Net leverage of 4.21x and interest cover of 2.72x leave little room for an earnings fall, and the 2026 improvement came from disposals that are now complete.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C4

Legacy PFAS cash calls and unquantified claims are the second weakness. Settlement payments run for 15 to 25 years, accrued litigation is USD 553 million, and large claims have no loss estimate, so the burden could outgrow the cost-sharing cap.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C16

Earnings concentration and volatility are the third weakness. Refrigerants supplied 72.25% of nine-month segment Adjusted EBITDA while their third-quarter earnings fell 30%, titanium dioxide earnings roughly halved in 2025 before recovering on price, and one titanium dioxide customer takes more than 20% of segment sales.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-02_cc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C15

The 2028 and 2029 maturity wall with a springing revolver is the fourth weakness. USD 1,427 million of payments fall in two years and the revolver matures early if the 2028 debt is not refinanced, so market access is the key refinancing risk, and one rating agency lowered its rating by one notch on July 17, 2026 and changed the outlook from negative to stable.

Governance history and an unread amendment are the fifth weakness. The 2024 review, open regulatory requests, a new class action in October 2026 and an amended annual report that was not supplied cap confidence in reported figures even though internal control was effective at year-end 2025.

### Company description

Chemours earns its cash from three product families sold into regulation-driven and cyclical markets: refrigerants and thermal solutions (Thermal & Specialized Solutions), titanium dioxide pigment (Titanium Technologies) and fluoropolymer materials (Advanced Performance Materials). In fiscal 2025 they were 35.57%, 41.82% and 21.75% of net sales of USD 5,808 million, and in the nine months to September 30, 2026 36.99%, 42.09% and 20.08%, so the sales mix is balanced but earnings are not. The business supports cash-flow visibility only in part: refrigerant sales follow a regulatory transition and a seasonal cooling season, titanium dioxide follows construction and packaging demand, and the company's own legacy-site liabilities attach to plants that remain in operation, which limits liquidity preservation and keeps refinancing confidence tied to earnings recovery.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C15
### Ownership and group structure

Chemours is a widely held public company with no controlling shareholder or sponsor identified, so there is no owner able to extract cash or to inject equity, and the proxy statement that would show large holders and board independence was not supplied. Debt sits at the parent and is guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries; the last guarantor-group summary covered fiscal 2025 and showed obligor net sales of 67.99% of group net sales, so at least 32.01% is earned outside the obligor group, a floor because intercompany sales inflate the obligor total. The 2034 notes carry a guarantee from a guarantor that no filing names, so the current perimeter is not established, and receivables are sold through a non-guarantor special purpose entity, so Structural priority must settle how claims rank.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 114; calculation C21
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is cyclical and policy-driven rather than recurring. Opteon sales jumped in 2025 on stationary air conditioning volumes tied to the AIM Act and fell in 2026 as the initial channel fill faded; nine-month net sales were flat as a 3% price gain offset a 3% volume fall, and Titanium Technologies lifted price 10% in the third quarter while volume rose 1%. Pricing power is real where regulation or quality limits substitutes, but the Opteon composition patents expire through the end of the decade and titanium dioxide demand is about 73.00% of nameplate capacity, so price gains depend on discipline rather than structure. Pigment grades are not fully substitutable because of quality consistency and specialty fluoropolymers are chosen for performance in demanding uses, but the filings give no retention or contract-duration data, so switching costs are not established; one pigment customer takes more than 20% of segment sales, which concentrates revenue risk in the segment meant to offset refrigerants.

### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margins are defended poorly under volume pressure. Cost of goods sold rose 4% in the third quarter on higher fixed costs and lower production rates while sales rose 3%, gross margin for nine months fell 0.50 percentage points to 16.16%, and Thermal & Specialized Solutions margin dropped to 27% from 35%; Titanium Technologies margin recovered to 13% from 4% on price. Energy is about 10% of titanium dioxide production cost and the company buys its titanium ore, chlorine and calcined petroleum coke from outside suppliers, with its own mines supplying under 10% of ore needs, so input shocks pass through unless priced. The chlorine plan for the DeLisle plant is not stated after the supply agreement ended in March 2026, and no fixed and variable cost split is supplied, so downside cost flexibility beyond capital spending and the dividend is not established.

### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital spending is flexible but is being held below depreciation. Twelve-month spending of USD 189 million is 59.25% of depreciation and amortization of USD 319 million, nine-month spending fell 14.29% and the outlook of USD 220 million to USD 230 million implies a larger fourth quarter. Conversion is low: free cash flow was 28.36% of adjusted EBITDA, interest expense takes 36.83% of adjusted EBITDA, supplier finance obligations rose to USD 151 million from USD 132 million at year-end 2025, and legacy settlements and a USD 90 million capitalised commitment under the Consent Decree sit on top. EBITDA therefore translates into limited cash for debt reduction, and the 2028 payments of USD 780 million are about 3.70x twelve-month free cash flow.

### Competitive forces

Rivalry is intense where capacity exceeds demand and moderate where patents protect. Refrigerant competitors include Solstice Advanced Materials, Arkema, Orbia, Daikin and Chinese producers, titanium dioxide competitors include Tronox, LB Group, Kronos and INEOS, and titanium dioxide demand is 73.00% of nameplate capacity, which caps price. New entry is limited by chloride process know-how, patents to the end of the decade for the main Opteon molecule and regulatory product approvals; substitutes are regulatory (the shift from older refrigerants) rather than competing products, and pigment grades are not fully substitutable. Buyers are fragmented at group level but concentrated in pigment, where the ten largest customers take more than 44% of sales, and supplier power is moderate: titanium ore comes from several suppliers on contracts and can be mixed across sites, chlorine and energy follow regional price cycles, and fluorspar and chlorinated organics are sourced from many suppliers. For creditors this means refrigerant earnings are protected only until patents lapse and pigment earnings depend on price discipline.

### Macro, regulatory and technology factors

These factors are material to credit. The AIM Act transition drove the 2025 Opteon surge and its 2026 fade, and the European fluorinated-gas rules support growth; PFAS regulation and litigation drive the settlements and the Consent Decree; trade policy and tariffs are managed through pricing and sourcing; construction and packaging demand set titanium dioxide volumes; and data centre cooling and semiconductor demand lift Performance solutions, whose nine-month net sales rose 7.32%. The telomer-based exit of a specialty business shows that regulation can strand products, and the annual report describes commercialisation of a next-generation refrigerant for data centre cooling as pending regulatory approvals.
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths are liquidity, scale across three segments, cost sharing with DuPont and Corteva, and restraint on distributions. Weaknesses are high leverage and thin interest cover, earnings concentrated in refrigerants, the 2028 and 2029 maturity wall, and legacy PFAS cash calls.

Opportunities are the continuing refrigerant transition, price recovery in titanium dioxide, data centre and semiconductor demand in advanced materials, and the outlook of net leverage below 4.2x. Threats are a faster fade in refrigerant volume, reversal of titanium dioxide price gains, PFAS claims that outrun the cost-sharing cap, tariffs and trade policy, and expiry of the Opteon composition patents by the end of the decade.

### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position is average: large and leading in two product families but exposed to price in both. Competitive advantage is average, resting on patents that expire through the end of the decade and process know-how whose cost position is management's own claim. Business diversification is average, because sales are balanced across segments while earnings depend on refrigerants. Cost and capex flexibility is average, with capital spending held below depreciation but largely fixed costs and a fixed environmental commitment. Margin stability is weak, shown by the swing in refrigerant and titanium dioxide margins. Free cash flow stability is weak, with negative free cash flow in fiscal 2024 and USD 211 million over the latest twelve months that includes escrowed receipts. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average: the market took the 2034 issue in March 2026 at a higher coupon, but one agency lowered its rating by one notch in July 2026 and the 2028 wall is close. Liquidity position is average: it is strong against the 2026 and 2027 payments but only adequate once the 2028 and 2029 payments are counted and with most cash held abroad. Financial policy and governance is average, with restrained distributions and no sponsor offset by the unresolved 2024 review and legal exposure.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 149; calculation C7; calculation C8

The main supports are liquidity, scale and cost sharing; the constraints are leverage, concentration and legacy cash calls; the trend is improving on leverage but flat on earnings; and the missing data are covenant levels, the amended annual report, credit documents, peer and market information, and cash interest for 2026.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months the company outlook is for fourth-quarter Adjusted EBITDA of USD 160 million to USD 185 million, a full-year range of USD 775 million to USD 800 million, capital spending of USD 220 million to USD 230 million and net leverage below 4.2x, with positive free cash flow in the fourth quarter. Tailwinds are titanium dioxide price momentum, order strength for Performance solutions products in data centre and semiconductor uses, and continued adoption of low global warming refrigerants under the AIM Act and European rules; headwinds are the fading stationary air conditioning aftermarket, annual settlement payments, tariffs, and the 2028 refinancing window opening within about 18 months. Over three to five years the Opteon patents lapse by the end of the decade, New Jersey payments are funded from escrow to 2030, and cost-sharing capacity is largely consumed, so the credit has to be sustained by earnings and market access rather than by disposals or counterparties.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-02_cc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 5; EX-99.1_2026-11-02_cc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 6; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C9; calculation C10; calculation C16
### Qualitative downside scenario

The scenario starts with titanium dioxide price gains fading because demand stays near 73.00% of capacity while refrigerant aftermarket volume keeps falling. The first operational break is lower volume at the refrigerant plants and weaker price realisation in pigment, which lifts unit cost because the cost base is largely fixed. Adjusted EBITDA falls by USD 100 million to USD 644 million, net leverage reaches 4.87x on net debt held at USD 3,135 million (USD 3,148.17 million pro forma for the declared dividend) and interest cover falls to 2.35x, while settlement payments continue. Management levers are capital spending, which is already below depreciation, the dividend of about USD 52.69 million a year and working capital; disposals are exhausted because the land sales are complete. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027 because only USD 68 million falls due in 2026 and 2027 and liquidity is about USD 1,431 million, but it would not hold leverage near current levels, and a refinancing in 2028 would be priced from a weaker position with the revolver's early maturity at stake. Observable triggers are fourth-quarter earnings below USD 160 million, pigment price reversal and revolver availability below USD 733 million.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); EX-99.1_2026-11-02_cc-ex99_1.htm.jsonl, page 5; calculation C3; calculation C6; calculation C12; calculation C14; calculation C17; calculation C18
### Overall credit view

Overall, Chemours presents an adequate but concentrated business profile supported by leading refrigerant and pigment positions, near-term liquidity that covers the 2026 and 2027 payments and cost sharing for legacy liabilities, but credit quality is constrained by high leverage, thin interest cover and unquantified PFAS exposure. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow is small after interest, capital spending and settlements. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on titanium dioxide pricing, refrigerant earnings holding up and the 2028 debt being addressed before the revolver's early-maturity window opens. The primary downside path is a fall in refrigerant and pigment earnings that lifts leverage while settlement payments continue. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and covenant levels, the amended annual report, the proxy statement, peer and market data, and cash interest for 2026. Top risk: refrigerant and titanium dioxide earnings falling before the 2028 refinancing.
